subject: Nanotechnology
title: Metalenses: Flat Optics
description: A micro-lesson that makes Metalenses: Flat Optics usable.

hook.text: A glass lens is thick, curved, and heavy — a metalens is flat, thin as paper, and focuses light just as well.

buildup.text: Nanopillars on a flat surface phase-shift incoming light differently at each point — bending the wavefront.

discovery.text: A single metalens can replace a stack of conventional lenses — eliminating aberrations with one engineered surface.

twist.text: Chromatic aberration is worse for metalenses — each wavelength sees a different phase shift from the pillars.

climax.text: Achromatic metalenses now correct for color — Harvard's design works across the full visible spectrum.

punchline.text: Nanopillars on a flat sheet replace a stack of curved glass lenses.

quiz.question: How do metalenses focus light without curvature?
options: They reflect light from a parabolic mirror hidden underneath
Nanopillars phase-shift light at each point to bend the wavefront like a curved lens
They use gravity to bend the light beam
